question: Simple interest on a sum for 5 years is equal to 20 percent of the principal. In how many years interest will be equal to the principal?
solution:
Given:

S.I. for 5 years = 20% of Principal

Formula used:

S.I. = (P × R × T)/100

where P → Principal

R → Rate of interest

T → Time period

Calculation:

Let the principle be Rs. P

According to the question,

⇒ (P × 5 × rate)/100 = 20% of P

⇒ rate = 4%

Now, let in t years the simple interest will be equal to the principal

⇒ Simple interest = (P × 4 × t)/100

⇒ P = (P × t)/25

∴ t = 25 years

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__Ratio of Principal to S.I. in 5 years = 100 : 20

Let the Principal be 100, so we are required to make S.I. = 100

⇒ S.I. of 20 = 5 years

⇒ S.I. of 100 = 5/20 × 100 = 25 years
